sections.h2: How do I reach the Manistee County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is at 415 Third Street, Manistee, MI 49660, in the county courthouse, and the phone is 231-723-2146. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to noon and 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. The register of deeds page links online land records, fee tables and the eRecording rules.

Manistee County is a Lake Michigan county in the northwest of the Lower Peninsula. It covers 1,281 square miles, of which 738 are water, and it was organized on February 13, 1855. The 2020 census counted 25,032 people. The city of Manistee is the seat, and the villages are Bear Lake, Copemish, Eastlake, Kaleva and Onekama. Roads that bring buyers and sellers in include US 31, M-22 along the shoreline, M-55 and M-115.

The county has thirteen state historical markers, including one for the Great Fire of 1871, and Manistee County-Blacker Airport northeast of the city offers direct flights to Chicago O'Hare. Whatever the town, a house in the county records here. Staff will help find and copy documents, but they will not run a title for you: the office says to use a title search company for that, and state law bars the staff from giving legal advice, including drafting or interpreting documents.

sections.h2: Can I mail a deed to Manistee County instead of dropping it off?
sections.html:
Yes. Since May 5, 2020 the register has said that in almost all situations it is acceptable and legal to mail completed documents to Register of Deeds, 415 3rd Street, Manistee, MI 49660. Call 231-723-2146 with questions about the procedure and cost before you send anything.

The office accepts all forms of payment, according to its FAQ, and the vault is open to the public for in-person copy requests. Online land records are a pay for view service covering 1978 forward, and a separate search covers 1856 to 1991. If you want a recorded copy or a certified copy returned, the office will forward it once copy fees are paid and you supply an addressed, stamped envelope.

Electronic recording has been available since December 14, 2017. The county's published business rules set the pace for e-filers:

  • Documents are processed between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, except county holidays.
  • Payment goes by ACH under the vendor agreements.
  • The register can reject any electronic document that breaks the Michigan Recording Act.
  • Vendors may add their own processing charges, but the register collects only the statutory recording fees.
  • Rule changes are posted 90 days before they take effect.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record and copy documents in Manistee County?
sections.html:
Recording a document costs $30 regardless of page count, under MCL 600.2567 as amended effective October 1, 2016. The exception is a document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument, which adds $3 for every instrument after the first.

Copy charges follow their own schedule. A real estate record copy starts at $7 for a two page document and adds $1 for each page after that, and the search fee is billed separately. The office states that payment must be received before documents are released.

Manistee County copy, certification and search fees from the Fees and Requirements page
ServiceFee

Real estate record copy, two pages$7, then $1 per added page
Plat copy$2 per page
Certification of a copy$5 per document
Search by name$0.50 per year, $5 minimum
State or federal tax lien certificate$3 per name each
UCC-11 certificate$6 per name

A certified copy must be made of the whole document to qualify.

sections.h2: Which Manistee County documents need the treasurer's certificate first?
sections.html:
Warranty deeds, any deed containing a covenant or warranty, land contracts, assignments of a land contract with a warranty clause and master deeds for condominiums all need a tax certificate before recording. The county cites MCL 211.135, and the certificate fee is $5.

The routing is specific to Manistee. You take the instrument to the County Treasurer's office first, and that office forwards the certified document with the fees to the Register of Deeds. The register does not send documents to the Treasurer, and an uncertified instrument is returned to the sender. Skipping the first step costs time at closing.

The statute asks for proof that taxes were paid for the five years before the date of the instrument. It also lets a county treasurer note that the current year's delinquent return was not yet available when a document is presented on or after March 1. A quitclaim deed or other conveyance with no warranty covenant does not need the certificate.

sections.h2: What must a Manistee County deed contain to be accepted?
sections.html:
The Fees and Requirements page lists fourteen conditions drawn from MCL 565.201 and related statutes. The ones that trip up sellers most often:

  • Original signatures with typed or printed names beneath, matching the name in the notary acknowledgment.
  • The grantee's street or post office address and the drafter's name and address.
  • A legible document in black ink, 10 point type, on white paper of at least 20 pound weight.
  • A 2.5 inch blank top margin on the first page, half inch on other edges, and a single statement on the first line naming the recordable event.
  • Pages between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches, attachments included.
  • Certified, sealed court orders, and a recorded death certificate when a survivor is named.

Manistee does not accept a death certificate attached to another document. It is recorded as a stand-alone document. If you are unsure whether your own deed qualifies, ask a title company or attorney to draft it, since the register cannot do so.

sections.h2: How are transfer tax and property taxes handled on a Manistee County sale?
sections.html:
When the value transferred is $100 or more, state and county transfer tax is due. The county rate is $0.55 for each $500 or fraction, and the state rate is $3.75 for each $500, which together make $4.30 per $500. The register's FAQ points to the legislature's exemption lists for transfers that owe nothing.

On a $180,000 sale that is 360 units of $500, so the county tax is $198, the state tax is $1,350 and the total is $1,548. Ask the title company to compute the figure from the actual price stated on the deed.

After the sale, the buyer must file a transfer notice with the local assessor within 45 days. Under MCL 211.27a, a transfer of ownership sets the taxable value to the state equalized value in the following year, so the new owner's bill may be higher than the seller's. Property tax questions go to the Manistee County Treasurer and the assessor for the city or township.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Manistee County?
faqs.a: Recording is $30 per document regardless of page count. A warranty deed also needs a $5 treasurer's tax certificate, and a document that assigns or discharges several instruments adds $3 for each one after the first.

faqs.q: What are the Manistee County Register of Deeds office hours?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to noon and from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. It closes for lunch each day, so plan a visit around that.

faqs.q: Does Manistee County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes, since December 14, 2017. E-recording documents are processed from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. on weekdays, payment goes by ACH, and the register collects only the statutory fees while vendors may add their own charges.

faqs.q: Can the Manistee County register of deeds do a title search for me?
faqs.a: No. Staff will help locate and copy documents, but the office says it cannot run title for anyone and you should contact a title search company. Online records are pay for view and run from 1978 forward, with an older search covering 1856 to 1991.

faqs.q: How much is Michigan transfer tax on a Manistee County home sale?
faqs.a: It is $4.30 for each $500 of value or fraction, which is $0.55 county plus $3.75 state. A $250,000 sale produces $2,150 in transfer tax, paid by the seller unless an exemption applies.
